name: The prophet's widow, and the pot of oil
charge: Borrowing not a few vessels, as the prophet said, and shutting the door
summary: A widow of the sons of the prophets had a creditor coming to take her two sons for bondmen and one pot of oil in the house. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels, not a few, shut the door, and pour. The oil stopped when the vessels did. She paid the debt and lived on the rest.
offense: A widow appealed to Elisha because her creditor was coming to take her two sons as bondmen. Her husband had feared the Lord, but his death had left an obligation her household could not meet. She possessed only a pot of oil (2 Kings 4:1-2). The need was both immediate and practical: the debt threatened the family that remained. Elisha told her to borrow empty vessels from her neighbours, not a few, and shut the door upon herself and her sons. She was to pour into the vessels and set aside those filled (2 Kings 4:3-4). Her preparation answered the word before the supply had multiplied. The sons whose removal she feared now helped bring the vessels to her.
judgment: She poured until every available vessel was full. When her son said there was no vessel more, the oil stayed (2 Kings 4:5-6). The account connects the extent of the filling with the vessels brought, without making the widow's poverty a limit upon the Lord's provision. Elisha directed her to sell the oil, pay the debt, and live with her children upon the rest (2 Kings 4:7). Deliverance did not mean pretending the debt had never existed. It supplied the means to discharge it and sustain the household afterward. The blessing reached the creditor's claim and the family's continuing need together, preserving the sons without exchanging one unresolved burden for another.

verses.text: Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the Lord: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.
And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.
Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.
And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.
So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.
And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.
And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:
But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile:
And then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.
A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
And they did all eat, and were filled.
And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.

entries.commentary: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha that her husband is dead, that her husband feared the Lord, and that the creditor has come to take her two sons to be bondmen. Because the husband died in debt, the creditor comes to take the sons to work off what is owed. Elisha asks what she has in the house, and she says nothing but a pot of oil. He tells her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors, not a few, then shut the door upon herself and her sons and pour oil into all the vessels. She pours out, and the oil continues until every vessel is full, and only then does the oil stay. Elisha tells her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live with her children on the rest. The empty vessels she borrowed from her people, the children of Israel, were filled through the spirit of the Lord.

Elisha passes through Shunem, where a great woman constrains him to eat bread, and as often as he passes by he turns in there to eat. She perceives that he is a holy man of God and tells her husband to make a little chamber on the wall with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick, so he may turn in whenever he comes. On a day when he rests in the chamber, Elisha wants to bless her and sends Gehazi to ask what may be done for her, whether she would be spoken for to the king or the captain of the host. She answers that she dwells among her own people. Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season. -

When the child is grown, he goes out to his father to the reapers and cries, my head, my head. His father has a lad carry him to his mother, and he sits on her knees till noon and then dies, from what seemed only a headache. She carries the child up and lays him on the bed of the man of God, the bed in the chamber she had made for Elisha, shuts the door, and goes out. She calls to her husband for a young man and an ass so she may run to the man of God, and though he asks why, since it is neither new moon nor sabbath, she answers, it shall be well. She rides to Elisha at Carmel, and when the man of God sees her afar off, he sends Gehazi to ask whether it is well with her, her husband, and the child, and she answers, it is well.

When she comes to Elisha at the hill, she catches him by the feet, and Gehazi comes near to thrust her away, but the man of God says let her alone, for her soul is vexed within her and the Lord has hid it from him. She says, did I desire a son of my lord, did I not say do not deceive me. Elisha tells Gehazi to gird up his loins, take his staff, greet no man on the way, and lay the staff on the face of the child. The mother says, as the Lord liveth and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee, so Elisha rises and follows her. Gehazi goes on before them and lays the staff on the face of the child, but there is neither voice nor hearing. He returns to tell Elisha the child is not awake.

When Elisha comes to the house, the child is dead, laid upon his bed. He goes in, shuts the door upon them both, and prays to the Lord. He goes up and lies upon the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretches himself upon the child, and the flesh of the child grows warm. He walks in the house to and fro, goes up and stretches himself upon him again, and the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Elisha calls Gehazi to call the Shunammite, and when she comes he tells her to take up her son. She falls at his feet, bows to the ground, takes up her son, and goes out. This is another act of the Most High through Elisha, restoring the child to life.

Elisha comes again to Gilgal, where there is a dearth in the land, and the sons of the prophets sit before him. He tells his servant to set on the great pot and seethe pottage for them. One goes out into the field to gather herbs, finds a wild vine, and gathers his lap full of wild gourds, shredding them into the pot, for they knew them not. As the men eat, they cry out, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot, and they cannot eat. Elisha tells them to bring meal, casts it into the pot, and says pour out for the people that they may eat, and there is no harm in the pot. He cures the poisoned food so the men may eat safely.

A man comes from Baal-shalisha and brings the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and full ears of corn in the husk. Elisha says, give to the people that they may eat. His servant asks how he should set this before a hundred men, but Elisha says again, give to the people, for thus saith the Lord, they shall eat and shall leave thereof. He sets it before them, and they eat and leave some, according to the word of the Lord.

When ye come into the land which I give you, six years thou shalt sow thy field and prune thy vineyard, but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the Lord: no sowing, no pruning, no reaping of that which groweth of its own accord. As we rest on the seventh day, the land rests the seventh year. Letting the land rest is harmony and balance on the earth, and the sabbath of the land is meat for thee, thy servants, the stranger, thy cattle, and the beasts in thy land. These land laws were given for the land of Israel; land bought in this captivity is not under the seventh year rest.

Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, forty and nine years; then shall thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement, throughout all your land. Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you, and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and every man unto his family. Neither sow, nor reap that which groweth of itself, for it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you.

If thou sell ought unto thy neighbour, or buyest ought of thy neighbour's hand, ye shall not oppress one another: according to the number of years after the jubile thou shalt buy, and according unto the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price, for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee. Thou shalt fear thy God, for I am the Lord your God; the price was reckoned honestly to the jubile so no man was oppressed.

Wherefore ye shall do my statutes and keep my judgments, and ye shall dwell in the land in safety, and the land shall yield her fruit, and ye shall eat your fill. If ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow nor gather in our increase: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years. The Most High answered the lack before it came: the sixth year would bring forth enough until the harvests of the ninth year came in, and ye shall sow the eighth year and eat yet of old fruit.

The land shall not be sold for ever, for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. Israel was not able to sell away any of the land for ever, because it is the holy land of the Most High, and in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land. If thy brother be waxen poor and hath sold away some of his possession, and any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold; or if the man himself be able, he may redeem it, or it goes out in the jubile and he returns to his possession. Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it meaning to buy it back. This is the prime example to reference for the curse that says no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem you. The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom; Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that.

If a man sell a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a whole year after it is sold; if it be not redeemed within the space of a full year, the house in the walled city is established for ever to him that bought it. But the houses of the villages which have no wall are counted as the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they go out in the jubile. Notwithstanding, the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel. Levi was not given any land; his portion was the offerings of the Lord, and the fields of the suburbs of their cities are their perpetual possession and may not be sold.

If thy brother be waxen poor and fallen in decay with thee, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee. The word stranger does not always mean a heathen; sometimes it is your own brother sojourning away from his land, and the context of the verse tells you which. Thy brother is thy neighbour and the children of thy people: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Brother, neighbour, and children of thy people all mean the same thing. Take thou no usury of him, or increase, but fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee. Usury is interest, a fee accumulating over time; thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase. Lending for the opportunity to make a profit off your own people is evil. I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan. The Most High is not the God of everybody: to bring Israel out He judged Egypt, and to give Israel Canaan He cast out the seven nations, greater and mightier than Israel, delivered them before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period.

If thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor and be sold unto thee, thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant, but as an hired servant and as a sojourner he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile; then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family and unto the possession of his fathers. The Hebrew servant serves six years, and in the seventh he goes out free for nothing; if he came in by himself he goes out by himself, and if he were married his wife goes out with him. That seventh year of release is that servant's jubile: a servant taken in 2012 goes out free in 2019, and one taken in 2019 goes out free in 2026. For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour, but shalt fear thy God; deal with him properly, for the Most High judges both the poor man and the one he serves.

Both thy bondmen and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids, and of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, and they shall be your possession. Ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever. But over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

If a sojourner or stranger wax rich by thee, and thy brother that dwelleth by him wax poor and sell himself unto the stranger, after that he is sold he may be redeemed again: one of his brethren may redeem him, either his uncle, or his uncle's son, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family; or if he be able, he may redeem himself, working as an hired servant and earning the price of his own freedom. Here again redeem means buy, as in buying a man out of slavery back to the position of freedom; and the price of his redemption was reckoned with him that bought him, according to the number of years from the year he was sold unto the year of jubile, as the time of an hired servant. If he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he and his children with him. For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. Everybody is not the servant of the Most High; the children of Israel are His servants, and this teaching identifies them today as the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and make thee an ark of wood; Moses made the ark of shittim wood and went up with the two tables in his hand. He wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments: twice the record says God wrote them, in [Deuteronomy 9:10](/bible/deuteronomy/9#v10) written with the finger of God and here again. That is why the law is so important; these are not merely the commandments of Moses, they are the laws of God, and breaking them brings judgment if you do not repent. We have to repent, keep the commandments, and be found blameless before the Lord when Christ returns. Moses put the tables in the ark which he had made, and there they be, as the Lord commanded.

Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest's office in his stead. At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name; wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren, the Lord is his inheritance. Levi ate well through the sacrifices the Lord set up: the Levites dwelt in the best areas, the suburbs, and lived in castles, because the Lord was their provider. All they had to do was teach Israel the commandments of God. But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

Moses stayed in the mount, according to the first time, forty days and forty nights, and the Lord hearkened unto him at that time also, and the Lord would not destroy thee. Arise, take thy journey before the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I sware unto their fathers.

And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee: here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel. Fear the Lord thy God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul: it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens is the Lord's thy God, the earth also; yet only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people, as it is this day. No other nation can lay claim to this: our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and the Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. Heavy scriptures right there.

Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward: that is what needs to be taught in the church, who we are really dealing with. Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: the Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life, so make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him.

He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment; love ye therefore the stranger, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? He is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out.

Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God; him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name. He is thy praise, and he is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and terrible things which thine eyes have seen. Thy fathers went down into Egypt with threescore and ten persons, and now the Lord thy God hath made thee as the stars of heaven for multitude. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

The cry is for the Most High to arise so His enemies are scattered and those that hate Him flee before Him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God. This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing. -

Let the righteous, those keeping the commandments, be glad and rejoice exceedingly before God. We are going to rejoice on our feast days, not oppressed by the enemy, serving the Lord without fear in the Kingdom. Sing praises to His name, extol Him that rideth upon the heavens by His name Yah, and rejoice before Him. The Lord has many titles as you read the scriptures. He is a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows; He sets the solitary in families and brings out those bound with chains, but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.

When the Most High went forth before His people and marched through the wilderness, the earth shook and the heavens dropped at His presence, and even Sinai itself was moved. Just as when we came out of Egypt, the Most High went before us in the wilderness and in the chariot; He always went before us. The scriptures talk about how when the Most High comes, the hailstorms come, the mountains tremble, and thunder and lightning appear. We serve the only true God, the God of Israel, the God of everybody. He sent a plentiful rain to confirm His inheritance when it was weary, and prepared of His goodness for the poor.

The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it. That is why you have different books of people that the Lord spoke to: Ezekiel, Jeremiah, and all the prophets in the company of Israel that published what God said. Kings of armies did flee, and she that tarried at home divided the spoil. Though they lay among the pots, yet shall they be as the wings of a dove covered with silver. -

The hill of Bashan is a high hill, but this is the hill which God desired to dwell in; yea, the Lord will dwell in it forever. The Most High dwells in Zion, in Jerusalem. That is why Christ said a city on a hill cannot be hidden; that is the city Jerusalem where the Lord dwells. The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels, the Lord among them as in Sinai. That is why in [Isaiah 66:15](/bible/isaiah/66#v15) He is coming back with the whirlwind. He has ascended on high, led captivity captive, and received gifts for men, even for the rebellious, that the Lord God might dwell among them.

Blessed be the Lord who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. As it says in [Lamentations 3](/bible/lamentations/3), His mercy is renewed every morning. He that is our God is the God of salvation, and unto God the Lord belong the issues of death. There is something we must understand: to the Lord belong the issues of death. That is why you see people get shot many times and still live, or go through things people wonder how they survived. When it is not your time you are not going, and when it is your time you are not staying. -

The Lord said He will bring His people again from Bashan and from the depths of the sea, that thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies. This is going into treading the winepress of the wrath of God, what you hear in the scriptures about treading grapes. The Lord said we are going to walk in the blood of our enemies, because the Lord is a man of war. Israel really does not know war in the sense we are in now; the scriptures talk about how the Lord is going to teach us to know war again.

They have seen the goings of the Most High, the goings of my God my king in the sanctuary. The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after, and among them were the damsels playing with timbrels, like a marching band with women playing instruments. Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord from the fountain of Israel. There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. These are the tribes of Israel, the sons of Jacob whose name was changed to Israel. -

Thy God hath commanded thy strength; strengthen, O God, that which Thou hast wrought for us because of Thy temple at Jerusalem, and kings shall bring presents unto thee. Rebuke the company of the spearmen, the multitude of the bulls, till everyone submit himself with pieces of silver; scatter the people that delight in war. Until they submit, paying taxes to us, we are going to make them submit and pay tribute. Princes shall come out of Egypt, and Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God.

Sing unto God ye kingdoms of the earth, to Him that rideth upon the heavens, who sends out His voice, and that a mighty voice. This is why in Revelation you hear the voice of many waters. God has a strong voice; His prophets have a strong voice. As men we speak with authority. On the streets the scripture says cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet. Ascribe strength unto God; His excellency is over Israel and His strength is in the clouds. The God of Israel gives strength and power unto His people. Blessed be God.

In his own country they are astonished at his wisdom and his mighty works, and then are offended at him because they know his family. A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. What was done to him is done to those teaching today: men who knew you before you repented ask who you think you are.

He could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk and healed them, and he marvelled because of their unbelief. Consider what that means. The unbelief of his own people was such that it made the son of the Most High marvel.

He sends them forth by two and two with power over unclean spirits, taking nothing for the journey but a staff. Whosoever will not receive you nor hear you, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. The word goes out whether they hear or whether they forbear, and that shaking of the dust seals the judgment.

Herod hears of him and says it is John, whom he beheaded, risen from the dead. John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

Herodias had a quarrel against John and would have killed him, but could not, for Herod feared him, knowing that he was a just man and an holy. When the oath is made, the daughter asks her mother what to ask, and is told, The head of John the Baptist. The king was exceeding sorry, but for his oath's sake he sent the executioner.

He was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things. Five loaves and two fishes feed five thousand men, and twelve baskets of fragments are taken up. He made them sit down by companies, in ranks by hundreds and by fifties. No man argued about where he was placed. The Most High is a God of order, and the eating came after the order.

He comes to them walking upon the sea, and they suppose it had been a spirit and cry out. These were fishermen; they knew what water does. They were sore amazed, for they considered not the miracle of the loaves, for their heart was hardened. Men can watch a thing done in front of them and still not take it to heart.
Wherever he entered, they laid the sick in the streets and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment, and as many as touched him were made whole.

text.text: Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the Lord: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.
And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.
Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.
And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.
So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.
And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.
Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.
And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant:
But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile:
And then shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.
A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.

And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
And they did all eat, and were filled.
And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.
